I'm not ready to start seriously saving for retirement but I find myself spending insane amounts on food and alcohol (which end up making me less happy anyhow). When I spend all of my paycheck on something good and have to live for a week or two on what I might normally spend in a single day I find myself to be happier and have something to show for it. But I'm very impulsive and clever and I do not trust myself with my own money.

What I need is some place where I can put my money, at will, and not be able to recover it (even at a loss or with a lot of effort) for a time period of my choosing.

Any ideas?
Is there a place I can invest my money, and not get it back easily, at will?

My credit union offers a Dream CD. You can deposit as much as you want a month ( minimum of $10) up to $100,000. There is a early withdrawal fee of 6 months if you do the 5 year term.

That or set up an auto transfer to another savings that you never look at.
Get YNAB. It might give you the motivation to not spend when you don't have to.

There are several places, some have been mentioned:

The first is to max out your work retirement savings program. This is all pre-tax dollars and Typically your employer will match some of your money (basically giving you free money). It never even Makes it to your bank.

Next, look into being able to open a Health Savings Account with your employer as well. More pre-tax dollars that comes out before you can touch anything, and it's money you can use for just about Anything health related (from insurance co-pays and deductibles to some over-the-counter stuff, depends on the HSA rules). The nice thing is that money in this account can be used, tax free, for the rest of your life. So even if you have awesome health/healthcare now, it could be a life-saver when you're 70.

Next are things you do once the money is in your hands. The most common are traditional IRA (you get to deduct that from your taxes, lowering your tax rate), Roth IRA (all post-tax), and if you want to set up a company for yourself, Sep-IRA (no limits on contributions unlike the others).

Obviously, throwing money at debt is a Fantastic idea if you have it ~ any money paid against the principle will shorten the length of the loan and result in your paying less overall.

Then you start getting into stuff where you can get money out without much trouble.. CD's, Money Markets, Stocks/investments, etc... If you have no willpower, these aren't really going to help. The best way to make them work for you though, is to hire a financial adviser (a fiduciary ~ research it). You give Them the money, they invest it on your behalf and you have no Direct control. You want it out, you go to them.... simply explain to the person you end up hiring that you need them to be your willpower for you. Set some ground-rules for when you can get money out, for what reasons, with what proof, etc...

Beyond that? it's all personal will-power. Sounds like you have impulse control issues (nothing wrong with it, but it can hurt you), so maybe some time with a psychologist to fix the problem rather than trying to find a bandaid. For a sorta work-around, if you're going to spend money make sure you are buying only the Absolute best. You want alcohol? Skip the well, and even the "top shelf" stuff and go for the limited stuff, the stuff where only 500 bottles were ever produced. Same with food... there's really No excuse to buy crappy experiences when you can afford better. Then, at least if you can't control your spending, at least you know you're getting the BEST money can buy. Maybe, with time, you'll realize that less just isn't worth buying and can break the cycle.

Whatever you do, the best of luck with it. I sure as hell wish I would have taken the money I was making in my 20's (best paying jobs I've ever had) and set it aside in savings. Instead I blew every cent on something or other and have nothing to show for it... not even any really Great experiences/memories.

I use smarty pig and have it automatically withdraw a set amount of money from my account each month. I also keep track of useless spending habits and deposit that amount each week so that those habits cost me twice as much money (this has helped me scale back on spending). Although it does take Smarty pig a few days to deposit and withdraw the money.
It sounds like you need a spouse or family member who understands your budget and manages your money for you.

Unfortunately that's not an option for me. Some people have pointed out that I could just start throwing it all at debt. Like, I have bad credit and a lot of my "debt" is really me getting robbed and so I just will not pay it. But I have other debt which matters a lot to me so I can just launch everything I've got at that.

Now the problem is pulling the trigger every time I get a paycheck and learning to live on a normal wage instead of spending all of my money. It sounds so easy but it wont be.

I think learning to manage your own money is worth the effort.

Making debt payments isn't an investment you can cash in the same as a bond or stock, but it does save money in the long run. You can count your interest payments on debt as the return on an "investment" to pay off the debt.
